newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-CINDERELLA JAGUARS UPSET BRONCOS 30-27.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-CINDERELLA JAGUARS UPSET BRONCOS 30-27.

text.p: In one of the biggest upsets in NFL history, the upstart Jacksonville Jaguars beat the Denver Broncos 30-27 in an American Conference playoff game on Saturday.
The Jaguars, in only their second year, came back from a 12-0 deficit behind two second-half touchdown passes by Mark Brunell and Natrone Means' punishing 140 years rushing that included a touchdown.
The Jaguars, will take their Cinderella story into the AFC Championship game next Sunday against the winner of the Pittsburgh-New England divisional playoff game.

In the third quarter, Brunell hit Keenan McCardell with a 31-yard touchdown pass in the third quarter and connected with Jimmy Smith on a 16-yard scoring play with 3:39 left in the fourth quarter to give Jacksonville a 30-20 lead.

Denver's John Elway, one of the greatest comeback quarterbacks in NFL history, began yet another rally. He marched the Broncos 80 yards in eight plays in just 1:49 and hit Ed McCaffrey with a 15-yard scoring pass with 1:50 left.
But the Broncos, who tied for the best record at 13-3 in the NFL in the regular season, failed to recover an on-side kick, and the Jaguars ran out the clock.

The Broncos scored two touchdowns in the first quarter, but missed an extra-point and a two-point conversion. The Jaguars responded with 13 second-quarter points to take the lead at intermission, 13-12.

Mike Hollis kicked field goals of 46 and 42 yards and Means scored on an eight-yard run in the second quarter for the Jaguars. Hollis added a 22-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter. He kicked three field goals in last week's 30-27 win at Buffalo.
Jacksonville closed the regular season with five straight wins to earn a playoff berth, and then went into Buffalo and became the first team to win a playoff game at Rich Stadium last Saturday.
"We should have put them away in the first half," Elway said.

"Our offensive line played great and opened the holes for me," Means said. "They left lanes wide open for me on some of thsose runs. We have a long way to go still, but I can see the Super Bowl at the end of the tunnel."

"Our line got it done, gave Mark (Brunell) time and pushed the Broncos back for Natrone," said Jaguars' offensive tackle Tony Boselli, rated by many people as the best lineman in the league. "We played smart and found out how good we are."
